meta.title: What You Don't See in a Finished Handmade Object
meta.excerpt: Beyond the polished surface lie materials, judgement, repetition, repair, and the many people whose work makes craft possible.
meta.headerQuote: The finished object is only the last visible chapter.
meta.author: Sree Jith
meta.alt: Landscape travel photograph introducing traditional making and material culture.

cover.alt: Landscape travel photograph introducing traditional making and material culture.

slides.title: The Material Had a Life Before This
slides.text: Clay came from earth; fibre grew through a season; wood took years. Every object begins with resources, landscapes, and choices about how they are sourced.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on the origins of natural craft materials.

slides.title: The Work Before the Work
slides.text: Sorting, washing, cutting, softening, or drying may take longer than the dramatic moment of making. Preparation is skill, not a footnote.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on preparing and sorting materials.

slides.title: A Tool Shaped by a Hand
slides.text: An old tool carries tiny adjustments: a smoother grip, a repaired edge, a balance that fits its maker. Knowledge can live in equipment.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on hand tools and accumulated craft knowledge.

slides.title: The Years Inside One Gesture
slides.text: A movement that looks effortless may have taken thousands of attempts. Apprenticeship teaches pressure, timing, and the moment to stop.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on repeated gestures learned through practice.

slides.title: The Mistakes You Never See
slides.text: The finished surface hides every correction. A skilled maker notices tension, alignment, or texture early enough to change course.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on craft judgment and careful correction.

slides.title: The Weather Enters the Workshop
slides.text: Heat, moisture, and drying time can alter materials. A craftsperson often works with the day’s conditions rather than against a rigid clock.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on the influence of weather and workshop conditions.

slides.title: No Object Is Entirely Solitary
slides.text: Suppliers, tool repairers, family members, and neighbouring specialists may all contribute. The maker’s name is important; the wider network matters too.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on the community behind individual craftsmanship.

slides.title: Time Must Have a Fair Price
slides.text: Admiration alone does not sustain a livelihood. Ask who made it, how long it took, and whether the price respects skilled labour.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on fair recognition of skilled craft labour.

slides.title: The Story Continues With You
slides.text: An object lives on through use, care, and repair. Buying thoughtfully is one way to respect the hands and resources behind it.
slides.alt: Portrait travel photograph accompanying a reflection on using and caring for handmade objects.
